steps.message:
The DER Program Office needs the written response to Northline Renewables' pre-application request dated 07/02/2025 on Feeder ALN-108, which asks for written confirmation of available capacity for a 3 MW pure-generation project, before the 08/15/2025 League response. Review 2025-07-02_PreApp_Request_ALN-108.pdf against 2025-07-14_Active_Queue_Report.xlsx and the DER Program records as they stand at 07/14/2025, including the Program Office's own case tracking, and issue the response the Program Office should send, with whatever it has to say about the figure. Record the call on the request's case in the case tracking, log any follow-up the response requires there, and close the case. Return your work as a single Word document, filed in the Program Office's correspondence folder in the document store, giving each determination with the basis you relied on, and the call made one way or the other.

Save it as /filesystem/ALN-108_PreApplication_Response.docx.
I'll start by exploring the filesystem to understand what's available.

NORTHLINE RENEWABLES LLC
1840 Ferngate Parkway, Suite 210 · Halston, Alleron 02HA · (612) 555-1826



                                    PRE-APPLICATION REQUEST
                                          Feeder Capacity Confirmation

 Date:           July 2, 2025
 To:             Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office
                 der.program@alleniom.com
 From:           Peter Ashford, Director of Project Development
                 Northline Renewables LLC
 Subject:        Pre-Application Request — 3 MW project on Feeder ALN-108


SUBMITTING PARTY

  Developer / Applicant           Northline Renewables LLC

  Business address                 1840 Ferngate Parkway, Suite 210, Halston, Alleron 02HA

  Primary contact                 Peter Ashford, Director of Project Development

  Telephone                       (612) 555-1826

  Email                           peter.ashford@northlinerenewables.com


REQUEST DETAILS
  Field                           Entry

  Date of submission              07/02/2025

  Addressed to                    Alleniom Utilities - DER Program Office

  Program inbox                   der.program@alleniom.com

  Subject                         Pre-Application Request - 3 MW project on Feeder ALN-108

  Requested feeder                ALN-108

  Substation area                 Elderpine substation service area, 13.2 kV distribution segment

  Requested project capacity      3 MW

  DER category                    Pure generation

  Interconnection type            Front-of-the-meter, export-only

  Anticipated technology
                                  Utility-scale photovoltaic array with central inverters; single-axis tracking, ground-mount


  Site status                     Land control secured; preliminary site engineering underway

  Anticipated in-service target   Q4 2026, subject to interconnection timing


STATEMENT OF REQUEST
Northline Renewables LLC is pleased to submit this pre-application request to Alleniom Utilities for feeder
capacity confirmation in advance of formal application. We are developing a 3 MW pure-generation
     photovoltaic project sited within the Elderpine substation service area, and have identified Feeder ALN-108
    as the intended point of interconnection.

    In preparation for this submittal, we have reviewed the Feeder Hosting Capacity Map published by
    Alleniom Utilities — Distribution Planning, which was the current published edition available at the time of
    our project sizing decisions.

    Per the published Hosting Capacity Map dated 05/15/2024, Feeder ALN-108 shows 3.0 MW of available
    capacity. We wish to proceed with a 3 MW project at the Elderpine substation service area and request
    confirmation.

    The published map lists ALN-108 as a pure-generation feeder segment at 13.2 kV, with the last planning
    study reflected as 04/2024. Our proposed project is fully aligned with the DER category shown for the
    feeder. Project capacity has been scoped at nameplate 3.0 MW so as to sit at, rather than above, the
    published available figure — with the express intent of avoiding a request that would exceed the feeder's
    stated headroom.

    We would appreciate written confirmation from the DER Program Office that the 3.0 MW published
    availability on Feeder ALN-108 remains current as of the date of this request, and guidance on the
    pre-application dialogue steps Alleniom would like to conduct prior to our filing of a formal interconnection
    application. Should Distribution Planning have updated feeder figures or study results that post-date the
    05/15/2024 publication, we would welcome the opportunity to receive that information so we can size the
    project accordingly.

    ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
     Project name (working)               Elderpine Solar I
     Nameplate DC                         approximately 3.9 MW-DC
     Nameplate AC (interconnection        3 MW-AC
     request)
     Inverter topology                    central inverters with plant-level SCADA-compatible controller
     Export profile                       100% export; no on-site load
     Environmental / permitting           interconnection critical path; permitting proceeding in parallel

    REQUESTED RESPONSE
1    Written confirmation of currently available capacity on Feeder ALN-108 for a pure-generation
     interconnection at the requested 3 MW nameplate.

2    Any known conditions, restrictions, or upgrade indications identified by Distribution Planning that would
     apply to a 3 MW project at this location.

3    Scheduling of a pre-application dialogue meeting with Distribution Planning and the DER Program Office
     at Alleniom's earliest convenience.

    Northline Renewables LLC appreciates the DER Program Office's consideration of this pre-application
    request. We remain available at the contact information above for any clarifying questions and stand ready
    to provide additional project detail as required.


    Respectfully submitted,
 /s/ Peter Ashford
Peter Ashford

Director of Project Development

Northline Renewables LLC

[P:] Feeder ALN-108 Planning Study — Post-Publication Update Q3 2024
[P:] Alleniom Utilities — Distribution Planning
[P:] DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com
[P:] Doc no. PLN-ALN-108-2024-10 · Rev 1 · Date 10/15/2024 · Owner: Distribution Planning
[P:] Prepared by: June Halloway, Distribution Planning Engineer
[P:] Contact: june.halloway@alleniom.com
[P:] 1. Purpose
[P:] This memorandum constitutes an interim update to the published Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map (HCM-2024-Q2, published 05/15/2024) with respect to Feeder ALN-108 (Elderpine substation, 13.2 kV, pure-generation category). It is issued between scheduled quarterly refreshes of the Hosting Capacity Map to record a material queue addition on the subject feeder that has occurred since the last published map release, so that Distribution Planning staff, applicant-facing correspondence, and pre-application dialogue may be informed of a working interim figure until the next full refresh cycle.
[P:] The scope of this document is limited to Feeder ALN-108. It does not modify the published values shown on any other feeder in HCM-2024-Q2, nor does it substitute for a formal feeder-level planning study in support of any specific interconnection application. Applicants and pre-application requesters seeking definitive feeder guidance for project scoping decisions should continue to consult Distribution Planning directly, and any project of consequential size on Feeder ALN-108 will require a full feeder-level planning study following the standard Alleniom Distribution Planning methodology.
[P:] 2. Baseline: Published Available Capacity
[P:] The Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map was published on 05/15/2024. The map reflects, on a per-feeder basis, the published available capacity value derived from the most recent completed planning study of record for each feeder as of the publication date, incorporating recorded peak and minimum load, existing interconnected DER of record at the time of the underlying study, and standard thermal, voltage, and protection screens.
[P:] For Feeder ALN-108, the published values on HCM-2024-Q2 are as follows:
[TABLE]
  | Attribute | Value
  | Feeder ID | ALN-108
  | Substation | Elderpine
  | Nominal voltage | 13.2 kV
  | DER category | Pure Generation
  | Last completed planning study | 04/2024
  | Published available capacity | 3.0 MW
  | Publication date | 05/15/2024
[/TABLE]
[P:] The 3.0 MW figure shown above is the baseline against which subsequent queue activity is netted for the purposes of this interim update. It remains, until the next scheduled quarterly refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map or an intervening full feeder re-study, the sole published available capacity of record for Feeder ALN-108.
[P:] 3. Post-Publication Queue Activity
[P:] Distribution Planning has reviewed the Active Queue Report as of the date of this document to identify interconnection applications assigned to Feeder ALN-108 that have been queued subsequent to publication of the Hosting Capacity Map. The following post-publication queue entry has been identified on Feeder ALN-108:
[TABLE]
  | Queue date | Feeder | Requested capacity (nameplate) | DER category
  | 09/18/2024 | ALN-108 | 1.2 MW | Pure Generation
[/TABLE]
[P:] The 1.2 MW project queued on 09/18/2024 is a pure-generation interconnection request, consistent with the DER category assigned to the feeder in HCM-2024-Q2. It represents the sole queue addition on Feeder ALN-108 identified in the Active Queue Report between the publication date of the map (05/15/2024) and the date of this study.
[P:] No other pending applications, executed interconnection service agreements, or in-service DER additions on Feeder ALN-108 have been identified since publication of HCM-2024-Q2 that would materially alter the baseline figure or the interim netted position stated below.
[P:] 4. Interim Netted Figure
[P:] Applying the post-publication queue entry identified in Section 3 against the published available capacity of record stated in Section 2, the interim netted available capacity figure for Feeder ALN-108 as of the date of this document is calculated as follows:
[P:] Interim available capacity: 3.0 MW − 1.2 MW = 1.8 MW.
[P:] This interim figure is provided as a working reference for Distribution Planning staff and for use in pre-application correspondence concerning Feeder ALN-108 where such correspondence is issued between quarterly refreshes of the Hosting Capacity Map. The figure is not a substitute for, and does not supersede, the published available capacity value of record on HCM-2024-Q2; the published value remains 3.0 MW until the next map republication.
[P:] The interim figure carries the following stated limitations:
[P:ListBullet] It reflects the state of the queue as of the date of this document only. Any subsequent queue additions, withdrawals, or reassignments affecting Feeder ALN-108 that post-date this study are not reflected in the figure above and will require Distribution Planning to reassess the interim position accordingly.
[P:ListBullet] It applies a straight-line nameplate netting against the published available capacity. A full feeder re-study, when performed, may yield a different available capacity value on Feeder ALN-108 depending on updated load recordings, revised existing-DER accounting, and the outcome of thermal, voltage, and protection screens as re-run against current data.
[P:ListBullet] The 1.2 MW queue entry is at the application/queue stage. Should that application be withdrawn or should its final capacity change following study or agreement negotiation, the interim netted figure would require corresponding adjustment.
[P:] 5. Recommendation
[P:] Distribution Planning recommends the following:
[P:ListNumber] Distribution Planning staff should treat 1.8 MW as the working interim available capacity for Feeder ALN-108 in any pre-application dialogue, applicant correspondence, or internal scoping analysis conducted between the date of this document and the next scheduled refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map. The published 3.0 MW figure on HCM-2024-Q2 remains the value of record for the map itself and should not be altered on the published map absent republication.
[P:ListNumber] A refreshed feeder-level planning study for Feeder ALN-108 should be scheduled to be undertaken in advance of, and its results incorporated into, the next full quarterly refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map. Feeder ALN-108 should be included among the feeders prioritized for re-study on the criteria stated in the map front matter: application date of pending queue entries, capacity requested relative to published available headroom, and DER category (pure generation is weighted more heavily against feeder headroom than net-metering behind-the-meter interconnections at equivalent nameplate).
[P:ListNumber] This document should be reissued or superseded if any further queue activity on Feeder ALN-108 arises before the next quarterly map refresh, so that the working interim figure remains accurate as of its date of issue. Distribution Planning will monitor the Active Queue Report accordingly.
[P:ListNumber] Applicants inquiring about Feeder ALN-108 between the date of this document and the next scheduled map republication should be directed to Distribution Planning for confirmation of the interim position before finalizing project sizing decisions, consistent with the general applicability note carried in the front matter of HCM-2024-Q2.

ALLENIOM UTILITIES
 APUC-Filed Interconnection Tariff
 §12 Interconnection Provisions
 Filed with the Alleron Public Utilities Commission
 Electric Tariff — Volume III · Original Sheet No. 214 · Effective: March 1, 2024
 Filed by: Alleniom Utilities · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA



 SECTION 12 — INTERCONNECTION OF DISTRIBUTED ENERGY
 RESOURCES
 §12.1 Applicability
 This section governs the interconnection to Alleniom Utilities' (the “Company”) distribution system
 of distributed energy resources (“DER”) within the Alleron service territory. Technical
 requirements, screens, study procedures, and equipment standards referenced herein are set out
 in the Company's DER Interconnection Standard (DIS-01) and companion standards, each of
 which is incorporated by reference. Nothing in this section shall be construed to modify or
 supersede any applicable safety, reliability, or protection requirement of the Company's
 engineering standards.




APUC Tariff Filing — Alleniom Utilities Electric Tariff, Vol. III, §12                     Page 1 of 6
 Alleniom Utilities — APUC-Filed Interconnection Tariff · §12 Interconnection   Volume III · Sheet No. 214




 §12.2 Scope of the DER Interconnection Program
 The DER Interconnection Program administered under this section applies to applications for DER
 interconnection at or above five hundred kilowatts (≥500 kW). Within the Program, DER shall be
 classified according to the DER Interconnection Standard as follows:

     (a) Commercial small-scale DER — five hundred kilowatts to one megawatt (500 kW – 1
        MW);
     (b) Medium-scale DER — one megawatt to five megawatts (1 MW – 5 MW).

 The Program scope threshold is ≥500 kW. DER below five hundred kilowatts (sub-500 kW),
 whether commercial or residential, are not administered under this section and shall instead be
 processed under the Company's Simplified Small-Systems Process, which is filed separately
 and is outside the DER Interconnection Program.

 Aggregation, controlled-capacity recognition, and shared point-of-interconnection eligibility are
 addressed in the DER Interconnection Standard and shall control the classification of any facility
 whose nameplate rating, aggregate site rating, or point of common coupling brings it within
 Program scope.




APUC Tariff Filing — Alleniom Utilities Electric Tariff, Vol. III, §12                       Page 2 of 6
 Alleniom Utilities — APUC-Filed Interconnection Tariff · §12 Interconnection             Volume III · Sheet No. 214




 §12.3 Application Intake and Queue Position
 A complete application shall establish the applicant's queue position as of the date the Company
 determines the application to be complete. Applications determined to be incomplete shall be
 returned with a written deficiency notice identifying each item requiring cure and the date by which
 cure is required. Queue position is not transferable between applications except as expressly
 provided in the DER Interconnection Standard.

 §12.4 Deemed Withdrawal Following Notice of Impending Withdrawal or Cancellation
 Upon issuance of a formal written Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation by the
 Company, the applicant shall have thirty (30) business days from the date of the notice to submit
 a substantive response curing the matter identified therein. If the applicant fails to respond within
 thirty (30) business days, the application shall be deemed withdrawn and shall be closed from the
 active queue without further action of the Company.

 For purposes of this section, “business days” shall exclude Saturdays, Sundays, and federal
 legal public holidays observed within the response window. Without limitation, the following
 federal holidays falling within response windows relevant to the current filing period are recognized
 as non-business days and shall not be counted:

   Holiday                                                               Observed Date

   Memorial Day                                                          05/26/2025

   Juneteenth National Independence Day                                  06/19/2025

   Independence Day                                                      07/04/2025

 The Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation shall be served in writing (certified mail or
 verified electronic delivery) and shall state the date of issuance, the response deadline computed
 under this section, and the consequence of non-response. The Company shall maintain a log of all
 notices issued, dates of service, and dispositions.




APUC Tariff Filing — Alleniom Utilities Electric Tariff, Vol. III, §12                                 Page 3 of 6
 Alleniom Utilities — APUC-Filed Interconnection Tariff · §12 Interconnection   Volume III · Sheet No. 214




 §12.5 Construction-Payment Defaults
 Where a construction work order or interconnection facilities invoice becomes payable and the
 customer has not remitted the amount due, the Company shall inform the customer in writing of
 the outstanding balance and shall issue a payment deadline of thirty (30) business days from
 the date of that written notice.

 For so long as the thirty (30) business-day payment deadline is running, the affected project shall
 remain on hold in the queue and shall NOT be deemed withdrawn. The construction-payment
 default procedure under this §12.5 is distinct from, and shall not be conflated with, the
 deemed-withdrawal procedure under §12.4; the two mechanisms have different triggers, different
 consequences, and different cure paths.

 Upon receipt of full payment prior to expiration of the deadline, the Company shall promptly
 release the hold and resume the affected work in queue order. If the deadline expires without
 payment, the Company may pursue such remedies as are available under the applicable
 Interconnection Service Agreement and this tariff, including, as a separate and subsequent step,
 issuance of a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under §12.4.




APUC Tariff Filing — Alleniom Utilities Electric Tariff, Vol. III, §12                       Page 4 of 6
 Alleniom Utilities — APUC-Filed Interconnection Tariff · §12 Interconnection       Volume III · Sheet No. 214




 §12.6 Interconnection Service Agreement
 Interconnection service shall commence only upon execution of an Interconnection Service
 Agreement (“ISA”) and the Company's written Permission to Operate. Material terms of an
 executed ISA, including but not limited to nameplate facility capacity and the designated point of
 interconnection, may not be modified by amendment. Post-execution changes to such material
 terms require withdrawal of the affected application and re-application in accordance with the DER
 Interconnection Standard.

 §12.7 Nondiscriminatory Queue-Order Processing of Applications
 Applications shall be processed by the Company in queue order on a nondiscriminatory basis.
 No applicant shall be advanced or disadvantaged in the processing sequence by reason of
 identity, affiliation, customer class, geography, or any other factor not expressly provided for in this
 tariff or in the DER Interconnection Standard.

 Scope note. This §12.7 applies to APPLICATION PROCESSING only — that is, to the
 sequencing of screening, technical review, study assignment, and issuance of interconnection
 determinations. Utility construction sequencing and the scheduling and allocation of constrained
 utility-owned      equipment       (including,   without  limitation,    remote     terminal    units,
 point-of-interconnection reclosers, and other supply-limited devices) are not governed by this
 section. Such matters are addressed under the Company's operating guidelines, including OG-17
 (Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline), which sets forth the criticality factors and
 prioritization criteria applicable to constrained equipment. Nothing in this §12.7 shall be construed
 to require the Company to sequence construction or equipment deployment in queue order where
 OG-17 or another operating guideline provides a different criticality-based ordering.




APUC Tariff Filing — Alleniom Utilities Electric Tariff, Vol. III, §12                           Page 5 of 6
 Alleniom Utilities — APUC-Filed Interconnection Tariff · §12 Interconnection          Volume III · Sheet No. 214




 §12.8 Reservation
 The Company reserves the right to seek modification of this section through filing with the Alleron
 Public Utilities Commission. Nothing in this tariff limits any authority reserved to the Commission
 by statute, rule, or order.



 Issued by: Director, Regulatory Affairs, Alleniom Utilities
 Filed pursuant to: Order of the Alleron Public Utilities Commission
 Docket / Sheet Reference: APUC — Alleniom Utilities Electric Tariff, Volume III, §12 (Interconnection
 Provisions)

 DER INTERCONNECTION STANDARD
  Doc no.               Rev         Effective date         Owner

  DIS-01                Rev 4       03/01/2024             Alleniom Standards Engineering — Evan Solberg

  Item                              Value

  Supersedes                        DIS-01 Rev 3 (12/01/2021)

  Basis                             IEEE 1547-2018

  Owner                             Alleniom Standards Engineering (Evan Solberg)

  Approved by                       Manager, Standards Engineering

  Distribution                      Alleniom DER Program Office; Interconnection Studies; DER Planning Group;
                                    SCADA/EMS Engineering; Regulatory Affairs; contracted developers on request

  Next scheduled review             03/01/2027


 Revision history
  Rev            Date             Summary

  Rev 1          06/01/2016       Initial issue.

  Rev 2          09/01/2018       Alignment with IEEE 1547-2018. Introduced Category 1/2/3 protective-equipment table.

  Rev 3          12/01/2021       Program-scope threshold set at 500 kW; added §3.4 aggregation.

  Rev 4          03/01/2024       Added §3.5 shared-POI eligibility; added §3.6 controlled-capacity recognition (UL 1741 / UL
                                  3141 PCS + Control Narrative); §7 restated to require withdrawal and reapplication for
                                  post-execution capacity or POI changes; Table 5-1 rewritten by category.




 §1 Purpose and Scope
 This standard establishes the technical and procedural requirements for interconnection of distributed energy
 resources (DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. It is based on IEEE 1547-2018 and applicable state
 interconnection rules filed with the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC), and it applies to all DER classes
 defined in §3.

 DIS-01 Rev 4 governs:

      • classification of DER facilities by aggregate nameplate capacity at the point of common coupling (§3);
      • eligibility to share an existing point of interconnection where legacy equipment is on site (§3.5);
      • recognition of a controlled operating limit below nameplate (§3.6);
      • protective and control equipment requirements by class and category (§5);



DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard                                                                            Page 1
                                                                                           DIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024



      • treatment of post-execution changes to executed interconnection service agreements (§7).
 This standard is read together with the APUC-filed interconnection tariff (§12). Where a topic is addressed by both
 this standard and the tariff, the tariff controls. Requirements for real-time monitoring and communications integration
 are established under TCS-02 and are not restated here except by cross-reference.




 §2 References
 The following documents are referenced within this standard. Unless otherwise noted, the latest published revision
 applies.

      • IEEE 1547-2018 — IEEE Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources
      with Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
      • DPS-07 Rev 2 — Alleniom Distribution Protection Standard (effective 09/15/2023). Establishes distribution
      protection requirements including protective devices at points of interconnection with export-capable in-scope
      facilities.
      • TCS-02 — Alleniom Telemetry & Communications Standard (effective 06/01/2021). Governs utility-owned RTU
      installation and SCADA telemetry for DER at and above the program-scope threshold; establishes the condition
      for permission to operate.
      • CEL-2025-Q2 — Alleniom Certified Equipment List (published 04/30/2025). Listing basis: UL 1741-SB and UL
      3141. The CEL front matter restates §3.6 of this standard.
      • ERP-9 — Alleniom Engineering Referral Procedure (Form ER-11). §3 routes any standards




 Definitions of terms used in this standard follow IEEE 1547-2018 and, where applicable, the definitions in the
 APUC-filed tariff. The terms aggregate nameplate capacity and point of common coupling (PCC) have the meanings
 assigned by IEEE 1547-2018 and reflected in Company practice. The terms point of interconnection (POI),
 export-capable, and pure-generation site are used in accordance with their ordinary meaning in utility
 interconnection practice.
 §3 DER Classification
 DER facilities are classified by aggregate nameplate capacity at the point of common coupling, in accordance with
 IEEE 1547-2018. Class thresholds, applicable review path, and equipment references are stated in Table 3-1.

 Commercial small-scale 500 kW–1 MW; medium-scale 1 MW–5 MW; program scope ≥500 kW; sub-500 kW DER
 (commercial and residential) is handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process, outside the DER Program.




DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard                                                                  Page 2
                                                                                                    DIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024



 Table 3-1 — DER classes

                              nameplate at PCC                                                              equipment
                                                                                                            reference

  Residential / small         < 500 kW           Simplified Small-Systems    Simplified small-systems       Table 5-1, Category
  commercial                                     Process — outside the       screening                      1

  Commercial small-scale      500 kW – 1 MW      In DER Program scope        Initial screening +            Table 5-1, Category

                                                 procedures

 The program-scope threshold is 500 kW. Facilities below 500 kW, whether commercial or residential in customer
 class, are routed to the Simplified Small-Systems Process and are not administered by the DER Program.

 §3.1 Determination of aggregate nameplate capacity
 Aggregate nameplate capacity is the sum of the manufacturer-rated ac output ratings of all generating equipment
 interconnected, or proposed to be interconnected, at a single point of common coupling. Manufacturer datasheets
 govern; derated or "operating" figures do not substitute for nameplate except as provided in §3.6.

 §3.2 Point of common coupling
 The point of common coupling is the point at which the DER facility is electrically connected to the Company's
 distribution system, as further defined in IEEE 1547-2018. The PCC is distinct from the point of interconnection (POI),
 the latter being the physical demarcation of Company-owned protective and metering equipment.

 §3.3 Determination on the basis of application
 Classification is determined on the facility as filed and as physically configured on site. Filing captions, project titles,
 and cover-letter characterizations do not alter classification; the connection diagram, the equipment schedule, and
 the address of record govern.

 §3.4 Aggregation
 Co-located DER behind the same point of common coupling counts toward one site total.

 Previously interconnected legacy equipment counts toward the aggregate regardless of the vintage of its permission
 to operate, regardless of whether it predates any current Alleniom standard, and regardless of the sequence or form
 in which subsequent applications are submitted at the same PCC. The aggregate governs the facility class and the
 resulting program-scope determination.

 An applicant proposing a new DER at a premises that already hosts DER shall identify the existing equipment on the
 application form and shall submit a one-line diagram showing the electrical relationship of the proposed equipment,
 the existing equipment, the customer load, the customer meter, and the PCC. Interconnection Studies verifies against
 the Company existing-DER register.

 §3.5 Shared-POI eligibility
 A new DER may share an existing POI only where the combined facility, including legacy equipment, can be brought
 to current monitoring/control standards; otherwise a separate POI and a new application are required. Where the
 existing system operates behind the meter, a new DER may instead be interconnected front-of-the-meter under its
 own service and POI, and is then evaluated on its own capacity without aggregation.




DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard                                                                           Page 3
                                                                                              DIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024



 The two dispositions available under §3.5 are:

   1. Shared POI, aggregated. The combined facility (legacy equipment plus proposed equipment) is brought to
      current monitoring/control standards as prescribed by TCS-02 and by Table 5-1 at the aggregate class. The
      applicant is responsible for the retrofit and for demonstrating retrofit feasibility to Interconnection Studies. Where
      feasibility is confirmed, the application proceeds at the aggregate capacity at the shared POI.
   2. Separate POI, non-aggregated front-of-the-meter alternative. Where the existing system operates behind
      the meter and the applicant elects to interconnect the new DER front-of-the-meter under a separate service and
      its own POI, the new DER is evaluated on its own capacity, without aggregation with the legacy equipment.
      Class placement, review path, and Table 5-1 category are determined from the new DER's capacity alone.
 Retrofit feasibility of legacy equipment is a factual question the Company will not decide from records alone; the
 applicant or its authorized developer must confirm feasibility in writing. Absent that confirmation, the shared-POI path
 under §3.5(1) is not available and the application is redirected to §3.5(2) or withdrawn.

 §3.6 Controlled-capacity recognition
 A limit below nameplate is recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification plus an approved Control
 Narrative — sufficient in themselves for recognition. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
 recognized limit is enforced as applicable: telemetry monitoring, and on pure-generation sites the POI recloser's ANSI
 32 directional-power element set to the recognized limit and tripping on violation.

 Required submissions. To have a controlled operating limit recognized in place of aggregate nameplate for
 program-scope and study purposes, the applicant shall submit both of the following:

   1. A valid Power Control System (PCS) certification issued under UL 1741 (including Supplement SB where
      applicable) and/or UL 3141, identifying the specific equipment arrangement at the applicant's site and the
      setpoint range.
   2. An approved Control Narrative — a written engineering document describing how the site's control system
      enforces the requested operating limit, including the sensed quantities, the response actions, the response
      times, the interlocks, and any allowable modes and their setpoint ceilings.
 These two documents, taken together, are sufficient in themselves to establish recognition of the controlled limit.
 Recognition establishes the capacity at which the facility is reviewed, classified, and studied.

 Enforcement backstops as arrangement provides. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
 recognized limit is enforced by the arrangement's existing equipment as follows:

      • Telemetry monitoring. For sites at or above the TCS-02 threshold, the Company's RTU-to-SCADA telemetry
      monitors real-power export at the point of interconnection against the recognized limit. Sustained deviation
      triggers investigation under TCS-02 and may result in a hold on permission to operate.
      • POI recloser directional-power element (pure-generation sites). On pure-generation sites — sites at which
      no customer load is served behind the point of common coupling — where a utility POI recloser is installed per
      Table 5-1 and DPS-07, the recloser's ANSI 32 directional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips
      the site on violation. The ANSI 32 element is inherently available in modern reclosers and does not require
      additional utility hardware.
 Enforcement provisions apply only as the site's arrangement provides them. Their absence at a particular site does
 not reopen the recognition determination once the two required submissions are on file.

 No controlled limit without submissions. In the absence of both a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification and
 an approved Control Narrative, nameplate governs for classification, program-scope determination, and study.

 Certified Equipment List. CEL-2025-Q2 restates this section in its front matter. Listing of a PCS on the current CEL
 does not by itself constitute recognition of a controlled limit for a particular site; the applicant's site-specific
 certification and Control Narrative are always required.

 §4 Screening and Study Process
 Applications in DER Program scope proceed through initial technical screening under Interconnection Studies.
 Facilities not passing initial screens may be evaluated under supplemental review per SRP-3 or advance to a system
 impact study. This standard does not restate SRP-3; the daytime minimum-load convention and other screen
 methodologies are prescribed there.

   2.    Table 5-1 addresses protective and control equipment. Monitoring and communications requirements are
        established under TCS-02.

        directional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips on violation.

 §6 Monitoring and Control
 Facilities at or above the TCS-02 program threshold shall provide real-time monitoring and control integration through
 a utility-owned RTU with SCADA telemetry as prescribed by TCS-02. Live telemetry to the Company system
 operations center is a condition of permission to operate. This standard does not restate TCS-02; refer to TCS-02 §5
 for the telemetry rule and to Alleniom system operations for RTU installation scheduling.

 Site-level control functions required by §3.6 (Power Control System recognition), by Table 5-1 (dedicated protection
 relay schemes, DER breaker arrangements), and by ERP-9 site determinations, together satisfy the
 control-integration expectations of this section as applied to the specific facility.

 §7 Capacity and Point-of-Interconnection Provisions
 Post-execution changes to executed ISA capacity or POI require withdrawal and reapplication; ISA edits are not
 permitted for capacity or POI changes.

 Scope. This section governs changes proposed after an interconnection service agreement has been executed by
 both parties. Prior to execution, ordinary revisions may be handled in the studies and drafting process without
 invoking this section.

 Principal parameters. Facility capacity and point of interconnection are principal parameters of the interconnection
 service agreement. Studies, protective-equipment scoping, and queue position each depend on these parameters as
 executed.

 Required path. A customer or developer seeking to change either the executed capacity or the executed point of
 interconnection after ISA execution shall:

   1. Submit a written request to withdraw the current application and terminate the executed ISA;
   2. File a new application at the desired capacity and, where applicable, the desired point of interconnection; and
   3. Accept the new queue position corresponding to the filing date of the new application.
 The new application is studied on its own facts. The withdrawal-and-reapplication path applies whether the requested
 change is an increase or a decrease in capacity and whether or not the requested change is characterized by the
 applicant as involving new or existing equipment.

 Other post-execution changes. Modifications to protective schemes, telemetry endpoints, equipment models within
 the same nameplate rating, and administrative items that do not alter capacity or POI are handled under the
 change-order provisions of the executed ISA and are not subject to this section.

 Downstream effects. The withdrawal of an executed ISA under this section releases any related utility equipment
 reservations and any related feeder headroom allocations, which are then available to subsequent applications in
 queue order. Studies previously performed at the withdrawn capacity are not carried forward; the new application
 receives a new study appropriate to its filed parameters.

 §8 Records and Compliance
 Interconnection Studies retains the application file, executed ISA, and study record for each in-scope facility for the
 retention period established by Regulatory Affairs. Standards Engineering maintains the current revision of this
 standard, the Certified Equipment List (CEL-2025-Q2 and subsequent editions), and the Engineering Referral
 Procedure (ERP-9) register of per-site determinations.

 standard and another Alleniom operating standard encountered in screening or study is referred to per-site
 engineering determination under ERP-9 §3.

[P:] Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office
[P:] 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com
[P:] Doc no. POL-QM-05  ·  Rev 3  ·  Date 03/15/2025  ·  Owner: DER Program Office
[P:] Queue Management & Withdrawal Policy
[P:] Applies to:  All DER Interconnection Program applications (≥500 kW) administered by the DER Program Office.
[P:] Supersedes:  POL-QM-05 Rev 2 (07/12/2023).
[P:] Owner:  DER Program Office.
[P:] Approving Authority:  Manager, Interconnection Studies.
[P:] §1  Purpose
[P:] This policy sets out the internal procedures by which the DER Program Office administers queue integrity and orderly withdrawal of applications from the active DER interconnection queue. It is intended to ensure that:
[P:] (a)	applications are closed only on a documented basis;
[P:] (b)	queue positions are established, retained, and released in a manner consistent with the Company's APUC-filed interconnection tariff (in particular §12.3, §12.4, and §12.6) and with the DER Interconnection Standard (DIS-01);
[P:] (c)	staff processing intake, screening, and case-management actions apply a single, uniform standard when an application appears stalled, abandoned, superseded, or replaced by a subsequent filing at the same site; and
[P:] (d)	the record supporting each queue action is complete and auditable.
[P:] Nothing in this policy modifies the tariff. Where any provision of this policy is read to conflict with the tariff or with an applicable engineering standard, the tariff and the standard control, and the conflict shall be referred to Regulatory Affairs for reconciliation.
[P:] §2  Withdrawal upon Customer Request
[P:] A stalled or abandoned application is closed only upon receipt of the customer's official withdrawal confirmation, provided in writing by letter or email. Where a new filing is submitted for the same site while a prior application remains open, the program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing; the new application takes its own queue date at time of filing. No queue-date inheritance is permitted.
[P:] §2.1  Scope of §2
[P:] This §2 governs closure of applications that have not been the subject of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under tariff §12.4. It applies where:
[P:] (a)	the customer has ceased substantive engagement with the program (whether by prolonged non-response, express indication of intent not to proceed, or otherwise);
[P:] (b)	the customer or an authorized developer has requested closure of an application without such a notice having issued; or
[P:] (c)	a new application is filed for the same site (as identified by service address, meter, or point of common coupling) while a prior application for that site remains in the active queue.
[P:] §2.2  Form of the Withdrawal Confirmation
[P:] To constitute an “official withdrawal confirmation” for purposes of this §2, the writing must:
[P:] (a)	be from the applicant of record (or from a person whose authority to act for the applicant has been established on the record — e.g., the developer named as the applicant's designated representative on the intake form);
[P:] (b)	be received by the DER Program Office by letter or email, addressed to der.program@alleniom.com or delivered to the DER Program Office at the letterhead address above;
[P:] (c)	identify the application by application identifier (PXA-YYYY-NNNN) and site; and
[P:] (d)	state expressly that the applicant withdraws the identified application.
[P:] Neither an oral communication (telephone, meeting, or voicemail), nor a status note recorded by staff, nor the mere filing of a new application at the same site, shall by itself constitute the official withdrawal confirmation required under this §2.
[P:] §2.3  Procedure — Stalled or Abandoned Application (Non-Notice Path)
[P:] Where staff identify an application within the scope of §2.1(a) or §2.1(b), the case handler shall:
[P:] 1.	Confirm the application's status in the active queue and document the basis for concluding that the application is stalled or abandoned;
[P:] 2.	Prepare and send a written communication (letter or email) to the applicant of record requesting the applicant's official withdrawal confirmation in the form specified in §2.2;
[P:] 3.	Log the request in the case file and in the queue-management system;
[P:] 4.	On receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, close the application and record the closure date, the closure basis (“§2 — customer request”), and the reference to the writing on file; and
[P:] 5.	Preserve the withdrawal writing in the case file in accordance with §4.
[P:] Absent receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, the application shall not be closed under this §2. If the applicant does not provide the confirmation and non-response persists, the case handler may refer the matter for issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under §3.
[P:] §2.4  Duplicate Filings at the Same Site
[P:] Where a new application is filed for the same site while a prior application for that site remains open in the queue:
[P:] (a)	The DER Program Office shall accept the new application in the ordinary course and shall assign the new application its own queue date determined as of the date the new application is determined to be complete. No queue-date inheritance is permitted between the prior and the new application.
[P:] (b)	The program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing in the form specified in §2.2. That request may be combined with the completeness/acknowledgement communication for the new application.
[P:] (c)	The prior application shall remain open in the queue until the official withdrawal confirmation is received, or until the prior application is otherwise closed by operation of §3 or under another tariff mechanism. The two applications shall not be merged, consolidated, or treated as continuations of a single filing.
[P:] (d)	Where the applicant states a preference or expectation that the earlier queue date apply to the new filing, staff shall respond in writing that the new application's queue date is fixed by §12.3 of the tariff and by this §2.4, and that closure of the prior application does not alter the queue date of the new application.
[P:] §2.5  Consistency with DIS-01 §7 and Tariff §12.6
[P:] Nothing in this §2 authorizes the use of a customer-requested withdrawal to reopen or amend an executed Interconnection Service Agreement. Post-execution changes to material terms of an ISA — including nameplate capacity and point of interconnection — require withdrawal-and-reapplication in accordance with DIS-01 §7 and tariff §12.6. A customer-requested withdrawal in that context establishes a new queue date for the successor application; no queue-date inheritance is permitted.
[P:] §3  Deemed Withdrawal (Procedural Restatement of Tariff §12.4)
[P:] Following issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation, if the applicant fails to respond within 30 business days, the application is deemed withdrawn.
[P:] §3.1  Relationship to the Tariff
[P:] This §3 is a procedural restatement, for internal use, of the deemed-withdrawal mechanism established by tariff §12.4. In the event of any inconsistency between this §3 and §12.4, the tariff controls. Staff shall consult §12.4 for the authoritative statement of the mechanism.
[P:] §3.2  Prerequisites to Issuance of a Notice
[P:] The DER Program Office shall not issue a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation unless:
[P:] (a)	the application has been open in the queue and staff have been unable to advance it because of the applicant's non-response or failure to supply required information or documentation;
[P:] (b)	at least one prior written follow-up has been sent to the applicant identifying the item or items required and requesting response by a stated date; and
[P:] (c)	the case handler has confirmed that the matter does not fall within the construction-payment default procedure under tariff §12.5, which is a distinct mechanism (project on hold, not withdrawn, while a 30-business-day payment deadline runs).
[P:] §3.3  Form and Service of the Notice
[P:] Every Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation shall:
[P:] (a)	be issued in writing on Alleniom Utilities letterhead;
[P:] (b)	be served by certified mail or by verified electronic delivery, in accordance with tariff §12.4;
[P:] (c)	identify the application by identifier and site;
[P:] (d)	state the item(s) requiring response;
[P:] (e)	state the date of issuance and the date on which the 30 business-day response window expires, computed under §3.4; and
[P:] (f)	state the consequence of non-response, i.e., that the application shall be deemed withdrawn and closed from the active queue without further action.
[P:] §3.4  Computation of 30 Business Days
[P:] For purposes of this §3 and of tariff §12.4:
[P:] (a)	“Business days” excludes Saturdays, Sundays, and federal legal public holidays observed within the response window;
[P:] (b)	Day 1 is the first business day after the date of issuance stated on the notice;
[P:] (c)	The following federal holidays observed within response windows relevant to the current filing period are recognized as non-business days and are not counted:
[TABLE]
  | Holiday | Observed Date
  | Memorial Day | 05/26/2025
  | Juneteenth National Independence Day | 06/19/2025
  | Independence Day | 07/04/2025
[/TABLE]
[P:] (d)	Where a response window straddles a federal holiday not listed above, the case handler shall exclude that holiday from the count and document the calculation in the case file.
[P:] §3.5  Effect of Non-Response
[P:] If the applicant fails to submit a substantive response curing the matter identified in the notice within 30 business days computed under §3.4, the application shall be deemed withdrawn as of the day following expiration of the window. The DER Program Office shall:
[P:] (a)	mark the application “deemed withdrawn — §12.4” in the queue-management system;
[P:] (b)	record the notice-issuance date, the expiration date, and the closure date in the withdrawal-notice log; and
[P:] (c)	preserve the notice, proof of service, and the closure entry in the case file in accordance with §4.
[P:] §3.6  Effect of Timely Response
[P:] A substantive response received on or before expiration of the 30 business-day window suspends the deemed-withdrawal consequence. The case handler shall evaluate the response and, if the identified matter is cured, release the application to resume processing. If the response is non-substantive or does not cure the identified matter, the case handler shall so document and, if warranted, issue a further follow-up or a subsequent Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation.
[P:] §3.7  Non-Substitution
[P:] Issuance of a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation is not a substitute for the customer-request path under §2, and the customer-request path under §2 is not a substitute for the deemed-withdrawal path under §3. Case handlers shall not use one mechanism to accomplish what should be effected under the other.
[P:] §4  Record-Keeping Requirements
[P:] §4.1  Case File Contents
[P:] For every application closed under §2 or §3, the DER Program Office shall maintain a case file containing, at minimum:
[P:] (a)	the original application and all completeness/acknowledgement communications;
[P:] (b)	for §2 closures: the writing (letter or email) requesting official withdrawal confirmation from the applicant; the applicant's official withdrawal confirmation (letter or email) as received; and any related correspondence bearing on the applicant's intent to withdraw;
[P:] (c)	for §3 closures: the prior follow-up correspondence relied upon under §3.2(b); the Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation as issued; proof of service (certified mail receipt or verified electronic delivery record); the 30 business-day computation worksheet; and any response received;
[P:] (d)	the queue-management system entry recording the closure basis, closure date, and (for §2 duplicate-filing cases) the queue-date determination applied to the successor application under §2.4(a); and
[P:] (e)	any related engineering or standards correspondence relied upon in the closure decision.
[P:] §4.2  Queue-Management System Entries
[P:] Every closure shall be recorded in the queue-management system with:
[P:] (a)	application identifier and site;
[P:] (b)	closure basis, expressed as one of: “§2 — customer request (letter)”, “§2 — customer request (email)”, “§2.4 — superseded by successor application”, “§12.4 — deemed withdrawn”, or such other codes as the DER Program Office may prescribe;
[P:] (c)	closure date;
[P:] (d)	case handler; and
[P:] (e)	reference to the writing(s) supporting the closure basis.
[P:] §4.3  Withdrawal-Notice Log
[P:] The DER Program Office shall maintain a running Withdrawal-Notice Log recording every Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation issued. The log shall include, at minimum: application identifier; site; date of issuance; method of service; response deadline (computed under §3.4); response received (date and disposition, if any); and closure date (if any). The log is subject to periodic reconciliation against the on-hold queue report; unreconciled entries shall be brought to the attention of the Manager, Interconnection Studies.
[P:] §4.4  Retention
[P:] Case files and log entries shall be retained in accordance with the Company's records retention schedule for regulated interconnection records. Records shall not be purged, redacted, or altered while an application remains open, while a response window under §3 is running, or while the closure is within the period during which reconsideration may be sought.
[P:] §4.5  Audit and Reporting
[P:] The Manager, Interconnection Studies shall be prepared, on request of Regulatory Affairs, to produce for any closed application: the closure basis; the writing(s) supporting the closure basis; the queue-date determination for any successor application; and, where applicable, the notice, proof of service, and 30 business-day computation. Reports to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission concerning queue closures shall be prepared from the withdrawal-notice log and the queue-management system entries described above.

import json, sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/tmp")
from mcpc import tool
def walk(path, depth=0, maxdepth=6):
    r = tool(8107, "list_files", {"request": {"path": path}})
    items = r.get("files") or r.get("items") or r.get("entries") or r
    if isinstance(items, dict):
        print("RAW:", json.dumps(items)[:1000]); return
    for it in items:
        name = it.get("name") or it.get("path")
        typ = it.get("type") or ("folder" if it.get("is_dir") else "file")
        p = it.get("path") or (path.rstrip("/") + "/" + name)
        print("  " * depth + f"- {name} [{typ}] {it.get('size','')} {it.get('modified', it.get('last_modified',''))}")
        if typ in ("folder", "directory", "dir") and depth < maxdepth:
            walk(p, depth + 1, maxdepth)
r = tool(8107, "list_files", {"request": {"path": "/"}})
print(json.dumps(r, indent=1)[:1500])
EOF

cd /tmp && python3 - <<'EOF'

        print(line); out.append((it['path'], it['type'], it['size']))

walk("/DER_Program")
json.dump(out, open("/tmp/nc_tree.json", "w"), indent=1)
EOF

arguments.command:
cd /filesystem && python3 - <<'EOF'
import json, os
tree = json.load(open("/tmp/nc_tree.json"))
for p, typ, size in tree:
    if typ != 'file': continue
    local = "/filesystem" + p[len("/DER_Program"):]
    ls = os.path.getsize(local) if os.path.exists(local) else None
    flag = "" if ls == size else "  <-- DIFF"
    print(f"{p}: nc={size} local={ls}{flag}")
# local files not in NC
ncset = set("/filesystem" + p[len("/DER_Program"):] for p, t, s in tree if t == 'file')
for root, d, files in os.walk("/filesystem"):
    for f in files:
        fp = os.path.join(root, f)
        if fp not in ncset: print("LOCAL ONLY:", fp)
EOF

import json, pandas as pd
d = json.load(open("/tmp/nc_active_queue.txt"))
content = d["content"]
# parse NC version
sheets = {}
cur = None
for line in content.split("\n"):
    if line.startswith("[Sheet: "):
        cur = line[8:-1]; sheets[cur] = []; continue
    if cur: sheets[cur].append(line.split("\t"))
print({k: len(v) for k, v in sheets.items()})
nc_rows = sheets["Active Queue"]
hdr = nc_rows[0]; nc = pd.DataFrame(nc_rows[1:], columns=hdr[:len(nc_rows[1])] if len(hdr)>=len(nc_rows[1]) else None)
nc = nc[nc["Project ID"].str.strip() != ""]
loc = pd.read_excel("/filesystem/Queue/2025-07-14_Active_Queue_Report.xlsx", sheet_name="Active Queue")
loc["Queue Date"] = loc["Queue Date"].astype(str)
nc["Queue Date"] = nc["Queue Date"].astype(str)
print("NC rows", len(nc), "local rows", len(loc))
m = loc.merge(nc, on="Project ID", how="outer", suffixes=("_loc", "_nc"), indicator=True)
print(m["_merge"].value_counts())
for c in ["Customer", "Site", "Capacity", "Feeder", "Queue Date", "Status"]:
    diff = m[(m["_merge"] == "both") & (m[c + "_loc"].astype(str).str.strip() != m[c + "_nc"].astype(str).str.strip())]
    if len(diff): print("DIFF in", c); print(diff[["Project ID", c + "_loc", c + "_nc"]].to_string())
print(m[m["_merge"] != "both"].to_string())
for k in sheets:
    if k not in ("Active Queue",):
        print("SHEET", k); [print("  ", r) for r in sheets[k]]
EOF

cd /filesystem && python3 - <<'EOF'
import pandas as pd, re, glob, os
oh = pd.read_excel("Queue/2025-07-14_On_Hold_Queue_Report.xlsx", sheet_name="Holds")
ids = set(oh["Project ID"].astype(str))
print("on-hold rows", len(oh))
# find feeder mentions for on-hold IDs across all text dumps
hits = {}
for f in glob.glob("/tmp/txt/*.txt"):
    if "On_Hold" in f: continue
    for line in open(f, errors="ignore"):
        for pid in re.findall(r"PXA-\d{4}-\d{4}", line):
            if pid in ids:
                feeders = re.findall(r"ALN-\d{3}", line)
                if feeders:
                    hits.setdefault(pid, set()).update((os.path.basename(f)[:45], fd) for fd in feeders)
for pid, s in sorted(hits.items()):
    print(pid, sorted(s))
print("on-hold IDs with feeder found:", len(hits))
# overlap between on-hold and active
act = pd.read_excel("Queue/2025-07-14_Active_Queue_Report.xlsx", sheet_name="Active Queue")
print("overlap active/on-hold:", sorted(ids & set(act["Project ID"])))
print(oh.head(3).to_string())
print(open("/tmp/txt/Queue__2025-07-14_On_Hold_Queue_Report.xlsx.txt").read()[-800:])
EOF

[P:] 	SUBJECT:	Backlog Review — Commercial DER Interconnection Program
[P:] The Alleron Municipal League's letter of 06/20/2025, submitted on behalf of fourteen member municipalities and school districts and copied to the APUC Energy Resources Division, is the trigger. We are not going to litigate its tone. We are going to fix the underlying condition that produced it.
[P:] Effective immediately, I am ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. The scope covers the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population — every application currently sitting in the program queue. I want each one accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action.
[P:] The following non-negotiable dates govern this work:
[P:] 1. 08/15/2025 — Formal written response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs owns the response letter. Harriet Ngoyi is the signatory. The response must address the League's five enumerated requests substantively and by project, not in aggregate.
[P:] 2. 09/10/2025 — APUC briefing. Queue accounting must be complete before we walk into that room. I will not brief the Commission on partial data. If a project's disposition is not final by 09/10/2025, I want the reason documented in the file, not explained at the podium.
[P:] Ground rules for every disposition reached in this review:
[P:ListBullet] Every disposition must be tariff-defensible. Cite the specific tariff section, standard, or operating guideline that supports the action. If the record does not support the disposition on paper, the disposition is not ready.
[P:ListBullet] Follow the noticing, payment-deadline, and hold-clearance procedures as they are written. Do not shortcut them, and do not extend them beyond what the tariff contemplates.
[P:ListBullet] Where standards or procedural conflicts exist, route them through the established referral process. Do not resolve them informally in the queue.
[P:ListBullet] No interim energization, no political prioritization, and no queue-date inheritance outside of what the tariff and program policy permit.
[P:] Reporting cadence. I want weekly progress updates to the VP office, in writing, every Friday by close of business beginning 07/04/2025. Format: counts by disposition category, exceptions requiring VP attention, and any item at risk of missing the 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025 dates. Meera, Ivo, and Marcus will support the DER Program Manager with the data pulls, study status, and telemetry/equipment inputs their groups own.
[P:] Escalate obstacles to me directly. I would rather field a problem on a Tuesday than read about it in a League follow-up letter.
[P:] /s/
[P:] Dana Whitcomb
[P:] Vice President, Distribution Operations
[P:] Alleniom Utilities

[P:] TO: DER Program Manager
[P:] CC: Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations
[P:] Meera Vellanki, Manager, Interconnection Studies
[P:] Ivo Grantham, Manager, DER Planning Group
[P:] FROM: Harriet Ngoyi, Director, Regulatory Affairs
[P:] DATE: 07/01/2025
[P:] SUBJECT: DER Backlog Review — Program Manager Tasking
[P:] 1. Confirmation of directive
[P:] This memorandum confirms and operationalizes the internal directive issued 06/27/2025 by Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations (DIR-2025-0627), ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. Regulatory Affairs accepts ownership of the external commitments arising from that directive and, by this memorandum, assigns the internal queue-cleanup work to the DER Program Manager.
[P:] The scope of the backlog review, as established by the VP, is the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population of the commercial DER program queue as of the anchor date. Every application is to be accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action. Nothing in this memorandum reduces, expands, or alters that scope.
[P:] 2. Governing deadlines
[P:] Two dates fix the outer boundary of this work and are not to be revisited without written concurrence from the VP office and Regulatory Affairs:
[P:ListBullet] 08/15/2025 — Response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs will issue the formal written response to the League's 06/20/2025 letter. The response will be substantive and project-specific, addressing the League's five enumerated requests on behalf of the fourteen member municipalities and school districts. Regulatory Affairs is the signatory; the DER Program Manager is responsible for delivering the underlying queue accounting on which the response will rest.
[P:ListBullet] 09/10/2025 — APUC briefing. The queue accounting must be complete and defensible in advance of the briefing to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission's Energy Resources Division. Regulatory Affairs will not present partial data to the Commission. Any application whose disposition remains open on 09/10/2025 must have a written reason on file, not an oral one.
[P:] Any interim regulatory information request the Division may issue in advance of the briefing will be answered from the same underlying record and will not create a separate work product for the Program Manager beyond timely disposition of the affected applications.
[P:] 3. Tasking of the DER Program Manager
[P:] The DER Program Manager is tasked, effective immediately, with producing the following queue-cleanup inputs. Each input is to be closed on the record — with the supporting document, tariff citation, standard, or operating guideline named in the file — before it is reported as complete.
[P:] 3.1 On-hold list dispositions. Work the current on-hold population by hold-reason category. For each project, determine the correct disposition under the applicable tariff provisions and program policy, and clear holds where the underlying reason has resolved. Cross-reference hold-reason categories against the relevant queue and financial records. Business-day counts must follow the standard business-day convention.
[P:] 3.2 Applications-intake corrections. Review the active queue for duplicate, ghost, and stale-status records. Where a customer has filed a new application at a site with a prior, silently abandoned filing, resolve the intake question in writing before either record is closed or merged. Queue-date assignment must follow the written policy.
[P:] 3.3 Standards-conflict routing. For every project currently sitting on a standards-clarification hold, determine and execute the correct disposition under applicable program standards and operating procedures.
[P:] 3.4 Equipment allocation. Convene the equipment-allocation determination for the sites that have completed construction and are awaiting utility-owned equipment. Rank the sites under the applicable equipment deployment prioritization guideline in accordance with its procedures, and match against the current supplier delivery schedule reported by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
[P:] 3.5 Aggregation determinations. For applications proposing new DER at sites that may host existing generation, apply the applicable aggregation provision before finalizing program-scope routing.
[P:] 3.6 Capacity verifications. For any application on abnormality hold due to a stated-vs-nameplate capacity discrepancy, verify the nameplate from the application's technical documentation and apply the applicable interconnection standard to any claimed operating limit below inverter nameplate.
[P:] 3.7 Hosting-capacity corrections. Before any capacity figure from the published hosting-capacity map is communicated externally, confirm that the figure reflects the current state of the affected feeder. A priority refresh is to be requested from Distribution Planning under the published refresh-prioritization criteria.
[P:] 3.8 Witness-test dispositions. Verify each inverter model against the applicable certified equipment list under the commissioning procedure in effect at the time of determination. Waiver eligibility is to be determined against the applicable certified equipment list.
[P:] 3.9 Supplemental-review reversals. Review any supplemental-review determination on file for consistency with current program procedures. Where the record requires revision, update the file and flag any prior memorandum that has been superseded accordingly.
[P:] 4. Reporting cadence
[P:] The DER Program Manager will provide weekly progress reports to Regulatory Affairs, with copy to the VP office, every Friday by close of business beginning 07/04/2025 and continuing through 09/12/2025. The weekly report will comprise:
[P:ListBullet] counts by disposition category, aligned to the categories in §3 above;
[P:ListBullet] items closed on the record during the reporting week, with the governing citation named;
[P:ListBullet] exceptions requiring Regulatory Affairs or VP attention, including any project at risk of missing 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025;
[P:ListBullet] forward-look for the following reporting week.
[P:] Reports are to be delivered in writing. Verbal updates do not substitute.
[P:] 5. General provisions
[P:] Every disposition reached under this tasking must be tariff-defensible on the face of the file. Cite the specific tariff section, standard, operating guideline, or bulletin that supports the action. Where the record does not support the disposition on paper, the disposition is not ready and is to be held rather than reported.
[P:] Follow the noticing, payment-deadline, and hold-clearance procedures as written. Standards or procedural conflicts route through the established referral process; they are not to be resolved informally in the queue. Queue-date treatment must remain within what the tariff and program policy permit.
[P:] Regulatory Affairs will coordinate with Interconnection Studies (Meera Vellanki) on queue and notice records, and with the DER Planning Group (Ivo Grantham) on study status, on any input required for the League response or the APUC briefing. The DER Program Manager remains the single point of accountability for the queue-cleanup inputs enumerated in §3.
[P:] Escalate obstacles to Regulatory Affairs in writing and, where the obstacle bears on the 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025 dates, to the VP office concurrently.
[P:] /s/
[P:] Harriet Ngoyi
[P:] Director, Regulatory Affairs
[P:] Alleniom Utilities

ALLERON MUNICIPAL LEAGUE
812 Larchmont Street · Cordwyn, Alleron 16CW · (651) 555-0244
The united voice of Alleron’s cities, towns, and school districts


Ref: AML-2025-0620-DER
June 20, 2025

Ms. Dana Whitcomb
Vice President, Distribution Operations
Alleniom Utilities
4200 Veldmere Boulevard
Halston, Alleron 01HA

RE: Escalation — DER Interconnection Program Delays Affecting Fourteen Municipalities and School
Districts
Dear Ms. Whitcomb:
On behalf of the Alleron Municipal League and the fourteen member communities identified below, I write to
convey our formal and collective concern regarding the continued and, in our view, unreasonable delays
affecting commercial-scale solar interconnection projects currently stalled within Alleniom Utilities’ Distributed
Energy Resource (DER) interconnection program. This letter follows repeated informal outreach by individual
member staff to your DER Program Office over the preceding several months, outreach which has not produced
the clarity or the timely progress our members need in order to close out their local capital projects.
The League is writing on behalf of 14 municipalities and school districts across the state of Alleron whose
commercial-scale solar projects — commissioned in good faith with voter-approved bond proceeds, adopted
capital budgets, energy-savings performance contracts, and in several instances state and federal grant awards
remain suspended in your interconnection queue awaiting energization. Among the affected members are:
     Brookfen Unified School District
     City of Elmsworth
     Darnwick Community School District
     Lockmere Community School District
     Cravenwood Community School District
     Town of Tresbay
     City of Marden Falls
     Town of Holcott
Additional League members with projects in the same posture have asked to be represented collectively through
this correspondence and are prepared to be identified upon request. Every one of these projects has been
reviewed and approved by the applicable local governing body, financed through public procurement, and
constructed by licensed contractors under permits issued by the relevant authority having jurisdiction.
The projects at issue are not speculative or exploratory. They range in size from approximately 500 kW to nearly
1 MW and are installed at public schools, municipal water and wastewater treatment plants, community centers,
public libraries, and other municipal facilities. In the great majority of cases construction is complete, mechanical
and electrical inspections have been closed out by local inspectors, and equipment has been standing
energized-ready — in some instances for a period now measured in months — pending only the Company’s
authorization to interconnect and place the systems into commercial operation. Each additional month of delay
defers budgeted operating savings, extends the payback horizon presented to our members’ councils and school
boards, and in the case of grant-funded projects places committed public funding at direct risk of forfeiture.
Our members are patient partners. They understand that the interconnection of distributed generation on the
Company’s distribution system requires careful technical review and, at times, coordination with equipment
procurement, feeder studies, and protection-scheme confirmation. They are willing to meet reasonable technical
requirements. What they are not able to accept — and what this League cannot accept on their behalf — is an
 extended period of silence, shifting explanations, and open-ended hold status without a clear articulation of what
is required, by whom, and by when.
Accordingly, and in a spirit of continued cooperation, the League respectfully requests the following from
Alleniom Utilities:
1. A full accounting of current queue status. For each identified League-member project, please provide the
    project’s assigned application number, current queue position, and complete processing history to date.
2. Hold reasons. For every project currently in a hold, pending, or suspended posture, please identify the
    specific reason for the hold, the party responsible for the next action, the information or resource required to
    release the hold, and the date the hold was established.
3. Expected energization dates. For each project, please provide the Company’s current best estimate of the
    date on which Permission to Operate will be issued, together with any intermediate milestone dates
    (studies, equipment delivery, witness testing, or telemetry acceptance) that inform that estimate.
4. A written response. We request the Company’s response in writing, addressed to the undersigned at the
    League’s Cordwyn office, within a reasonable period consistent with the urgency our members’ councils
    and school boards are attaching to this matter.
5. A meeting. We request an in-person meeting between the Company’s senior distribution leadership, the
    League’s executive office, and designated representatives of the affected members, to be scheduled at the
    Company’s offices in Halston or at a mutually convenient location in Cordwyn at the Company’s preference.
    The League is prepared to convene our members on short notice once the Company proposes a date.
For your awareness, a copy of this letter has been provided to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC),
Energy Resources Division, for the Division’s information. The League has taken this step not as a matter of
confrontation but out of a good-faith obligation to keep the Commission’s staff apprised of a program-level
concern affecting a substantial number of Alleron public entities across multiple service territories within the
Company’s distribution footprint. It remains our strong preference to resolve this matter directly with Alleniom
Utilities.
The League and its members recognize that Alleniom Utilities has been a constructive counterparty on many
prior initiatives, and we approach this escalation with the expectation that the Company shares our interest in
restoring predictable, transparent processing timelines to the DER program. Our members’ communities have
invested public funds, published expected in-service dates to their constituents, and in several cases entered
into contractual arrangements predicated on interconnection occurring by dates that are now past. The credibility
of local government energy planning across Alleron is meaningfully bound up in the outcome, and we are
confident the Company understands the seriousness with which we, our elected officials, and our school boards
regard it.
I would be grateful for the courtesy of an acknowledgment of receipt at your earliest convenience, and I remain
available to discuss any aspect of the foregoing at the telephone number above. Thank you for your prompt
attention to this matter.

Respectfully submitted,


Alden Pryce
